title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Dynamics — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State Newton's three laws of motion. Give an example of each.
questions.solution:
**First Law (Inertia):** A body at rest stays at rest, and a body in motion continues in a straight line at constant velocity unless acted on by an external force. *Example: passengers in a bus lurch forward when brakes are applied.*

**Second Law:** F = ma. *Example: a cricket ball accelerates when a bat applies force.*

**Third Law:** For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. *Example: a rocket pushes gas downward and is propelled upward.*
questions.knowledgeNote: The three laws hold in inertial frames only; the third implies momentum and force conservation.
questions.answer: **First law (inertia):** a body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted on by a net external force — *example:* passengers lurch forward when a bus brakes (their bodies keep the previous motion). **Second law:** the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied net force and in its direction: **F = ma** — *example:* the same push accelerates an empty trolley more than a loaded one. **Third law (action–reaction):** to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction — *example:* a rocket rises by pushing exhaust gases down; the gases push the rocket up (also: walking — you push the ground backward, the ground pushes you forward). **Deep point:** the three laws are one story — the first defines force's absence (inertia), the second measures it (F = ma), the third says it never acts alone (pairs on different bodies).
